---
title: "Package architecture"
---

This page is for people who want to read, modify, or extend spDBL. It maps
the workflow functions to the code that implements them. For the statistical
model, see `vignette("calibration-details")` and
[Banerjee et al. (2025)](https://jmlr.org/papers/v26/22-0896.html).

## Layers

| Layer | Files | What lives there |
|---|---|---|
| Workflow API | `R/func_wrapper.R`, `R/calibration_prepare.R`, `R/calibration_fit.R` | `prepare_data()`, `emulator_learn()`, `emulator_predict()`, `calibration_prepare()`, `calibration_validate()`, `calibration_fit()`, `calibration_predict()`, and the S3 methods for `spDBL_calibration` |
| Dynamic linear model kernels | `R/func_FF.R`, `R/func_BS.R`, `R/func_FFBS.R` | Forward filter, backward sampler, posterior sampling and prediction for each covariance model |
| Out of core | `R/func_FF.R` (`FF_bigdata_R()`), `R/func_bigdata.R` | Filter, smoother and exact predictor that stream CSV blocks from disk |
| Compiled kernels | `src/FF.cpp`, `src/BS.cpp`, `src/rmn.cpp` (RcppEigen) | One forward-filter step, one backward-smoothing step, matrix-normal draws |
| Calibration internals | `R/calibration_recover.R`, `inst/stan/*.stan` | Stan data assembly, the two Stan programs, R reference log densities, recovery of discrepancy and field draws |
| Distributions | `R/func_MNIW.R`, `R/func_MNIW_sampler.R`, `R/func_lppd_ana.R` | MNIW/MNIG updates and samplers, matrix-T density, one-step log predictive densities |
| Data and design construction | `R/func_gen_data.R`, `R/func_generate_grid_Dan.R` | Kernels, autoregressive design matrices, episode partitioning, grid traversal, synthetic data |
| Simulator and legacy helpers | `R/func_calibrate.R` | The SIR reaction–diffusion simulator (`SIR()`, `gen_pde()`) and helpers from the original research code |
| Plotting | `R/func_plot.R` | Heatmap panels and interval summaries |

## Covariance models and naming

The emulator is a matrix-variate dynamic linear model. Its right (spatial)
covariance has three forms, and kernel functions carry a matching suffix:

| Model | Suffix | Example functions | Available in `emulator_learn()` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Inverse-Wishart Σ | none | `FF()`, `FFBS()`, `FFBS_sampling()` | `covariance = "iw"` (default) |
| σ² R, R fixed | `_sigma2R` | `FF_sigma2R()`, `FFBS_sigma2R()`, `FFBS_sampling_sigma2R()` | `covariance = "sigma2R"` (required for calibration) |
| Identity | `_I` | `FF_I()`, `FFBS_I()`, `FFBS_sampling_I()` | no; kernel functions only |

## Emulation: what `emulator_learn()` does

1. Validates the grid (`Nx`, `Ny`), the blocking (`episode_window` must divide
   `Nx`), and the kernel settings.
2. Builds two exponential kernels with range `3 / (gp_tune * max distance)`:
   `V` over simulator inputs and `R_episode` over the sites of one spatial
   block. The full-grid `R_field` (S × S) is not formed unless supplied; only
   calibration uses it, and `.cal_R_field()` builds it at the observed sites.
3. Splits each time step's field into `B = Nx / episode_window` spatial blocks
   (`generate.grid.rowsnake()`). Every (time, block) pair is one *episode* of
   the dynamic model; this is the dynamic transfer-learning partition.
4. Builds the autoregressive design for every episode with
   `gen_F_ls_AR1_EP()` or `gen_F_ls_AR2_EP()`, unless `F_ls_train` is given.
5. Runs forward filtering and backward smoothing: `FFBS()` or
   `FFBS_sigma2R()`. The inverse-Wishart forward step is in C++
   (`FF_1step_cpp`); the σ² R step is in R (`FF_1step_R_sigma2R()`); every
   backward step calls `BS_1step_cpp`.
6. Draws `nsam` posterior samples with `FFBS_sampling()` or
   `FFBS_sampling_sigma2R()`. `sampling = "marginal"` draws each episode's
   smoothed marginal given a shared covariance draw; `sampling = "joint"` draws
   whole coefficient paths.
7. Returns an object of class `spDBL_emulator` with `para_ffbs` (filtering and
   smoothing moments), `res_ffbs` (posterior draws), and `setup` (every
   setting and design needed for prediction).

`emulator_predict()` calls `FFBS_predict_exact()` (default) or
`FFBS_predict_MC()` (`MC = TRUE`), then maps episodes back to the time × space
layout with `recover_from_EP_exact()` or `recover_from_EP_MC()`. Given the
output of `calibration_prepare()`, it predicts with GP-interpolated design rows
instead, so no new simulator runs are needed.

## Calibration: from emulator to posterior

1. `calibration_prepare()` requires a `"sigma2R"` emulator. It reuses the
   emulator's draws or resamples them (`sample_calibration_emulator()`), then
   `make_offline_calibration_input()` fits the design-row GP
   (`fit_offline_ar2()`, squared exponential with one length scale per input)
   and caches Cholesky factors. Result: class `spDBL_calibration_input`.
   `predict_calibration()` turns one coefficient draw into the field mean and
   covariance at an input. With `design_uncertainty = TRUE` (the default) the
   covariance includes the design GP's error, as a rank-N factor per time
   (`.cal_design_factors()`).
2. `calibration_validate()` compares these PDE-free predictions with held-out
   simulations.
3. `calibration_fit()` validates the settings, compiles or loads the Stan
   program (`.cal_stan_model()`), and calls `fit_calibration_rstan()`. That
   function runs one conditional Stan fit per emulator draw and pools an equal
   number of samples from each fit. Result: class `spDBL_calibration`, with
   `summary()`, `print()` and `plot()` methods.
4. `calibration_predict()` recovers discrepancy paths
   (`recover_calibration_discrepancy()`) and field draws
   (`recover_calibration_predictions()`).

There are two Stan programs in `inst/stan/`:

* `calibration_marginal.stan`, the default (`marginal_discrepancy = TRUE`),
  integrates the discrepancy states out with a Kalman filter.
* `calibration_offline.stan` samples the discrepancy innovations explicitly.

Both integrate out the emulator field analytically. R reference
implementations of the same log densities (`calibration_log_density()`,
`calibration_marginal_log_density()`) let the tests check the Stan code.

## Large grids out of core

For grids too large to hold every episode in memory, three functions stream
CSV blocks from disk (`R/func_FF.R`, `R/func_bigdata.R`):

1. `FF_bigdata_R()` filters forward and writes each time step's filtered
   moments, all blocks side by side, to one set of CSV files.
2. `BS_bigdata_R()` reads those files backwards, one time step at a time, and
   writes the smoothed moments.
3. `FFBS_predict_bigdata_R()` streams each block's responses, designs and
   smoothed means, and writes one prediction file per time step.

Memory holds one time step of moments and one data block at a time. The tests
check all three against the in-memory `FF()`, `BS()` and
`FFBS_predict_exact()`. Prediction needs every training run in each block
(`bnrow = fnrow`), as `emulator_learn()` arranges them.

## Reproducibility mechanisms

* Every function that takes a `seed` sets it locally and restores the caller's
  random-number state on exit (`.cal_seed()`).
* Compiled Stan models are cached in memory and on disk
  (`tools::R_user_dir("spDBL", "cache")`, or `cache_dir`). The cache key
  combines the Stan file's MD5 hash and the R, rstan, StanHeaders and platform
  versions, so editing a Stan file triggers a recompile.
* `calibration_fit(checkpoint_dir = ...)` saves each conditional fit to disk
  as it finishes. Nothing reloads these files automatically; a rerun starts
  again from the first emulator draw.
* `calibration_fit()` records `execution_only = TRUE` when there is no
  warmup or fewer than two post-warmup iterations, as with `iter = 1`.
  `iter` has no default, so every analysis states its sampler settings.

## Extending spDBL

* **A new covariance model** needs a one-step forward filter, a sampler for
  the covariance, an `FFBS_*()`/`FFBS_sampling_*()` pair, and a new
  `covariance` option in `emulator_learn()`. The `_sigma2R` functions are the
  closest template.
* **A new input kernel**: the exponential kernel and its range heuristic are
  defined inside `emulator_learn()`; `FFBS_predict_exact()` and the
  calibration code read the stored `phi_para`, `gp_sigma2`, and `gp_tau2`.
* **A new sampling backend**: `calibration_fit(backend = )` accepts only
  `"rstan"` today. The backend-specific code is `.cal_stan_model()` and
  `fit_calibration_rstan()`.

## Tests

The tests are in `tests/testthat/`. The calibration tests compare the
Gaussian conditioning, the Stan log densities, and the pooled sampler with
independent R calculations. Tests that compile Stan are skipped unless
`SPDBL_RUN_STAN_TESTS=true`; the coverage workflow on GitHub Actions turns
them on. See the
[contributing guide](https://github.com/xiangchen-stat/spDBL/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for how to run tests and coverage locally.

## Known limitations

* The out-of-core path covers filtering, smoothing and exact (mean)
  prediction. Posterior sampling and calibration work in memory.
* The `delta` (discount) argument of the one-step filters is accepted but not
  used.
* Calibration supports the σ² R emulator only, with a fixed discrepancy
  covariance scale `U`, complete observations, and the training grid and
  times.
* The design-row error is treated as independent across observation times,
  although it is in fact persistent; see `vignette("calibration-details")`.
